memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: From Aroer on the rim of the Arnon Gorge, and from the town in the gorge, even as far as Gilead, not one town was too strong for us. The Lord our God gave us all of them. But in accordance with the command of the Lord our God, you did not encroach on any of the land of the Ammonites, neither the land along the course of the Jabbok nor that around the towns in the hills. - Deut 2:36-37 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses summarises the conquest of Sihon's territory with a striking statement: "not one town was too strong for us. The Lord our God gave us all of them." The same people who, decades earlier, had trembled before walled cities and giants, now found that no town could stand against them. What had changed? Not their strength, but their willingness to trust and follow God. When God gives, no obstacle is too strong.

Remember the earlier generation at Kadesh, who looked at the tall walls and the powerful peoples and shrank back in fear, refusing to enter. Now their children, going forward in faith, discovered that those very obstacles were nothing before the power of God. The giants that had terrified their parents were no match for the Lord who fought for them. The difference between defeat and victory was trust.

This encourages us to reframe the obstacles in our own lives. What looks impossibly strong to us is not too strong for God. The walls that make us want to shrink back, the challenges that seem insurmountable — none of them can stand against the Lord's power when He is with us. Our task is not to be stronger than our obstacles, but to trust the God who is stronger than all of them.

Notice too that even in victory, Israel obeyed God's limits, not encroaching on Ammonite land. Their success did not make them greedy or presumptuous; they still walked in obedience. This is the balance: bold in faith to face every God-appointed challenge, yet humble in obedience to God's boundaries. With God, no obstacle is too strong; and in Christ, we are more than conquerors through Him who loved us (Rom 8:37). Face your walls in the strength of the Lord.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What "town too strong" are you facing that God is bigger than?
2. How does trusting God change the way you see your obstacles?
3. How can you be bold in faith yet humble in obedience, as Israel was here?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Mighty God, nothing is too strong for You. Help me to face my obstacles trusting Your power rather than my own strength, bold in faith yet humble in obedience, knowing that in Christ I am more than a conqueror. Amen.
